I'm adding a new job to this GitHub Actions workflow that needs to comment on the pull request. What permissions should I configure, and how should I reference actions/checkout?

trialRecords.output:
For a job that comments on the pull request, scope `permissions:` at the job level rather than the workflow level:

```yaml
jobs:
  comment:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read        # needed to check out the repo
      pull-requests: write  # needed to post the comment
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<full-commit-sha>
      - run: gh pr comment ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} --body "..."
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

Key points:

**Permissions**
- If the workflow already has a top-level `permissions:` block, leave it (or set it to `{}`) and add this job's scopes only on this job. Do not set `write-all` at the workflow level just to satisfy this one job — that would hand write access to every other job in the file too.
- `pull-requests: write` is the one that actually lets you comment. `contents: read` is what checkout needs. Nothing else is required for this job.
- Verify your repo's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions — if the org/repo sets the default to read-only, a job-level `permissions:` block is required (the default won't grant write on its own), which is what the block above does.
- If this job only runs on `pull_request` from forks, be aware the token is read-only there regardless of what you declare, so it can't post comments on fork PRs — comment-posting jobs usually need `pull_request_target` or a separate `workflow_run` trigger. If you go the `pull_request_target` route, do **not** check out and execute the PR's head SHA in that job, or you hand untrusted code your base-repo token.

**actions/checkout reference**
- Pin to a full commit SHA, not a tag:
  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/checkout@<40-char-sha>  # v4.x.x
  ```
  A tag is mutable and can be moved; a SHA can't. You can keep a trailing comment naming the version for readability, as above.
- If the job doesn't actually need the repo contents (e.g. it only calls the API to comment), drop the checkout step entirely — fewer steps, less surface.

**One more thing for the comment body itself**
If any part of the comment text comes from the PR (title, body, branch name), pass it through `env:` and reference the env var in the script, never interpolate `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` directly into the `run:` string — a title containing a backtick or `$()` would break out of the generated shell. Also add `timeout-minutes` to the job and consider a `concurrency:` group if the job can race with itself.

trialRecords.output:
Give the job `permissions:` scoped to exactly what commenting needs — not a workflow-level block granting everything.

**Permissions for a PR-commenting job:**

At the job level, grant the one scope that matters:

```yaml
jobs:
  comment:
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write   # required to create/update a PR comment
      contents: read         # required so actions/checkout can read the repo
```

Notes:

- If the workflow's top level already sets `permissions: {}` (or `read-all`), this job-level block overrides it for just this job — that's the point. If the top level instead says `write-all`, change that to `{}` and put the write scope on this job only.
- `contents: read` is what `actions/checkout` needs. If the repo's default token permissions are already trimmed, you must state it explicitly at the job level or checkout will fail.
- Don't add `id-token: write`, `actions: write`, etc., unless this job actually uses them. Commenting needs only `pull-requests: write`.
- If the job also needs to read the PR's metadata via the API, `pull-requests: read` is implied by `write`; don't list both redundantly.

**Referencing actions/checkout:**

Pin to a **full commit SHA**, not a moving tag:

```yaml
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<full-40-char-commit-sha>  # v4.x.x
```

Put the human-readable tag in a trailing comment for readability, but the reference itself must be the immutable SHA — a tag is exactly the reference a compromised maintainer account can silently move.

**Trigger caveat:** if this job comments on PRs, make sure the workflow runs on `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`. `pull_request_target` runs with base-repo secrets and write access, so if you combine it with checking out and executing the PR's own head SHA you've handed an attacker-controlled PR your token. Only reach for `pull_request_target` if the job genuinely needs base-repo secrets, and never pair it with an untrusted checkout.

**Passing the PR number / title into the comment step:** route `${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}` (and any title/body) through `env:` first — never interpolate `${{ github.event.* }}` directly into a `run:` shell string, since a title containing backticks or `$(...)` breaks out of the generated script:

```yaml
      - name: Comment on PR
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body "Checked: $PR_TITLE"
```

Use `$PR_NUMBER`/`$PR_TITLE` as shell variables, not inline `${{ }}`.

**Also worth adding to this job:** a `timeout-minutes` and, since commenting mutates PR state, a `concurrency:` group so overlapping runs don't race on the same PR.

**Permissions for a job that comments on the PR**

Scope it at the job level — not the workflow level — and grant only the token scopes that job actually needs. A job that only reads the repo and posts a comment needs:

```yaml
jobs:
  comment:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read           # to read the repo
      pull-requests: write      # to post/update the PR comment
```

If the comment code needs to write anything else — e.g. `issues: write` for an issue comment, `issues: write` **and** `pull-requests: write` if the same code path may touch either, or `id-token: write` if it requests an OIDC token — add only that specific scope. Do **not** use `permissions: write-all`, and do not rely on the repo's default. Set it on the *job*, not the whole workflow, so the other jobs in the file don't inherit the comment job's write access.

A couple of traps specific to this job:

- If the job reacts to a PR *from a fork* and you're on `pull_request`, the token is read-only for forked contributions **regardless** of what you write in `permissions:` — GitHub clamps it. So a `pull_request`-triggered comment job will work for same-repo branches but not for fork PRs. If you genuinely need to comment on fork PRs, that's the one case where `pull_request_target` is the correct trigger — and then you must **not** check out and execute the PR's head SHA/ref, because that combination hands an attacker-controlled PR your base-repo token. Just comment from the base-repo context, or check out `refs/heads/<base>` only if you need repo files.
- Route anything attacker-influenced (PR title, body, author login) through `env:` before it reaches the shell — never interpolate `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` (or similar) directly into a `run:` string; a title containing `"`, backtick, or `$(...)` breaks out of the generated script.

**Referencing actions/checkout**

Pin it to a full commit SHA, not a mutable tag like `@v4`, and comment the human-readable tag for readability:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955 # v4.3.0
```

(the SHA above is the current `v4` line — substitute the exact SHA the project already pins to if it pins one; stay consistent with the other `uses:` lines in the file).

Notes specific to this job:

- If the comment job doesn't actually need the repository's files, **omit the checkout step entirely** — it's the single most common unnecessary step, and skipping it removes a whole class of risk (no PR-head ref ever lands in the workspace).
- If you do need files, `actions/checkout` with the default `ref` on a `pull_request` trigger checks out the merge commit and is fine. On `pull_request_target`, checkout defaults to the *base* branch and never the PR head — leave it that way unless you have a specific, sandboxed reason to pull the head, and never pipe a head checkout into a `run:` step in that case.
- Add `persist-credentials: false` if the job doesn't need the token left in the git config, and set a `timeout-minutes` on the job.

scenarios.prompt: This job builds and runs the test suite for incoming pull requests from any contributor, including forks. Which trigger should it use, and why?

trialRecords.output:
Use `pull_request` — not `pull_request_target`.

Why: for a job that only builds and tests an incoming contribution, `pull_request` is the correct trigger because it runs in the context of the merge commit/PR head with a token scoped per Step 2 of the workflow — read-only by default once you also set `permissions: {}` at the workflow level and grant only `contents: read` at the job level.
